title: Ring maps of finite presentation
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. A *presentation* of $A$ over $R$ is a pair of integers $n,m\ge0$, polynomials $f_1,\dots,f_m\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and an isomorphism of $R$-algebras $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_m)\cong A$ (equivalently, a surjective $R$-algebra map $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]\to A$ whose kernel is the ideal generated by $f_1,\dots,f_m$). The ring map $R\to A$ is *of finite presentation*, or $A$ is a *finitely presented $R$-algebra*, if $A$ has a presentation over $R$.
